first_impression.reaction: Googled 'wedding processional songs' because my fiancee asked me to sort the ceremony music. I expected a ranked 'top 40' with no reasoning. It isn't ranked, and every entry has a date, composer or album I can check. Jumped to the FAQ first, then the practical bits on timing and live versus recorded. Useful, low on fluff. A few entries end mid-sentence though, and the planner pitch turns up before the destination section that is meant to justify it.

journey.quote: These 40 wedding processional songs are grouped by style rather than ranked: classical, church and hymns, instrumental, and modern.
journey.reaction: Good. No fake 'number one song of all time' claim. Just grouped.

journey.quote: It is the processional. If the wedding party and the couple walk to different music, the couple's piece is often called the entrance or bridal entrance song.
journey.reaction: Straight answer, first line. That's what I came for.

journey.section: How long should a processional song be?
journey.quote: Long enough to cover the walk, which depends on your aisle and the number of people walking. Time it at the rehearsal.
journey.reaction: Honest. Doesn't pretend there's a magic number. The fade note is practical too.

journey.quote: Recorded music gives you the exact version you love, and needs a reliable sound system, someone to press play and a back-up copy.
journey.reaction: Trade-offs spelled out. But no idea what a quartet costs versus a speaker hire. That's the actual decision.

journey.section: 7. Spring (from The Four Seasons), Antonio Vivaldi
journey.quote: The opening movement is bright and sunny,
journey.reaction: Sentence just stops. If nobody proofread this, what else wasn't checked?

journey.quote: Its simple, repeating melody is easy to time
journey.reaction: Another one cut off. Second time now. Sloppy for a brand calling itself premium.

journey.quote: It has a light waltz feel and a gentle wit
journey.reaction: Third unfinished line. That's a pattern, not a typo.

journey.section: What can you walk down the aisle to in a church?
journey.quote: Whether a particular piece, or any secular song, can be used in your church is the church's decision, so ask your officiant or music director early.
journey.reaction: Admits a limitation instead of promising anything goes. Fair.

journey.quote: If you are marrying overseas, Wedded Concierge plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: Sales line dropped in before the destination section has made any case. And 'payments' again: do you take a cut?

journey.section: How does a destination ceremony change your processional music?
journey.quote: Music permissions: Does the venue have the permissions it needs for live or recorded music at your ceremony, and are there any sound limits or curfews?
journey.reaction: Good question list. This is the kind of thing that bites you on the day. I'd actually use it.

journey.section: How does a destination ceremony change your processional music?
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: In writing is right. Still nothing on what the Advisor costs or who pays them.

journey.section: Plan the rest of the day's music
journey.quote: When you are ready, tell us your date, your guest list and the feeling you want, and a Wedded Advisor will plan it with you as your single point of contact through Wedded Concierge.
journey.reaction: 'The feeling you want.' I want a fee schedule. Same silence as every planner site.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a string quartet, pianist or soloist cost for a ceremony versus hiring a sound system, in AUD?
How many minutes does a typical processional actually take for, say, a 6-person wedding party on a 20 m aisle?
Do music licensing fees apply to recorded songs at an overseas venue, and who pays them?
Does Wedded Concierge source the musicians, and is their fee passed through at cost or marked up? (deferred business detail)
How is the Wedded Wonderland fee calculated, and what's a realistic 'from AUD' figure? (deferred business detail)
Show me a real ceremony you've planned with the music line in the actual budget. (deferred business detail)

would_share_with: My fiancee: the FAQ on bridal entrance songs and the 'one piece for the party, a different one for the couple' tip
Our Reddit thread: the destination question list (power, sound limits, music permissions, wet-weather plan)

cta_reaction.quote: To plan the music, the venue and every other moment of a destination wedding with one person, start with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: Decent free song list, honest about church rules and timing, but it's a music article with no cost figures and nothing on fees or commissions. Nothing here tells me what I'd be paying for, so I'd keep comparing.

top_3_changes: Finish the three truncated sentences (Vivaldi's Spring, River Flows in You, Married Life). Unfinished lines cost trust with careful readers.
Move the mid-article Concierge line below the destination question list, so the pitch follows the evidence.

Add a sourced cost signal for live musicians versus recorded music (or say 'not published'), and near the closing CTA state how the fee works and whether supplier commissions apply (deferred business detail).
